102_single_reference_analysis.question: Does any SINGLE prior-art reference teach ALL limitations of the M6 candidate?
M6_limitations: L2: active backflow prevention (mechanical one-way valve)
L3: dual-zone coating (anti-fouling CSF side + anti-thrombogenic venous side)

single_reference_assessment.El_Shafi: Teaches L2 (anti-reflux via flow direction) but NOT L1 (surgical, not endovascular), NOT L3 (no coating), NOT L4 (no surface treatment). Does NOT teach all limitations → 102 does NOT apply.
single_reference_assessment.Sinushunt: Teaches L2 (pressure-based anti-reflux) but NOT L1, L3, L4, L5. Does NOT teach all → 102 does NOT apply.
single_reference_assessment.1975_venous: Teaches anti-stagnation concept but NOT L1, L3, L4, L5. 102 does NOT apply.
single_reference_assessment.fibrous_web_2026: Teaches L4 (anti-adhesion surface) but NOT L1 (ventricular, not venous), NOT L2 (no anti-reflux), NOT L3 (no dual-zone). 102 does NOT apply.
single_reference_assessment.conclusion_102: NO single reference teaches ALL M6 limitations. 102 rejection would FAIL. BUT: this does NOT establish patentability — 103 is the real threat.

103_combination_obviousness_analysis.question: Is the COMBINATION of M6 limitations obvious from the prior art?

combination_analysis.El_Shafi_teaches: venous CSF drainage + anti-reflux/flow-direction + anti-stagnation/clotting prevention
combination_analysis.modern_anti_fouling_teaches: surface coating for CSF shunts (PVP, fibrous web, etc.)
combination_analysis.motivation_to_combine: HIGH — a patent examiner could argue: (1) El-Shafei established venous-shunt anti-reflux; (2) modern coatings are known for shunts; (3) anti-thrombogenic coatings are known for blood-contacting devices; (4) combining them for an endovascular venous shunt is obvious
combination_analysis.potential_103_rejection: STRONG — the combination of known elements (venous anti-reflux + anti-fouling coating + anti-thrombogenic coating + endovascular deployment) may be deemed obvious under 103
counter_arguments: Endovascular deployment creates DIFFERENT flow topology than surgical — not merely a different access method
The dual-zone coating (anti-fouling CSF side + anti-thrombogenic venous side) is NOT taught by any single reference
Historical venous shunts did NOT use surface coatings — the combination is not merely additive
The biological turnover model shows the combination produces non-additive effects under specific conditions
combination_analysis.counter_argument_weakness: The non-additive effect was NOT robust (43% Monte Carlo). The counter-arguments rest on the combination producing an unexpected effect, but that effect is not reliably demonstrated.

103_combination_obviousness_analysis.conclusion_103: 103 rejection is a MATERIAL THREAT. The combination may be deemed obvious. The counter-argument rests on unexpected effect, but the effect is not robust. Patent counsel REQUIRED.

part_3_102_103_analysis.implication_for_architecture: The 102/103 analysis reveals that M6's differentiation rests on COMBINATION + ENDOVASCULAR + DUAL-ZONE. But 103 obviousness is a strong threat because each element is known. The architecture must produce a GENUINELY NEW PHYSICAL EFFECT, not merely combine known elements. The next candidate should be built from the FAILURE PHYSICS (venous-interface causal chain), not from combining existing anti-fouling + anti-reflux components.

failure_physics_chain.step_1_blood_entry_probability: How likely is blood to enter the shunt?
failure_physics_chain.step_2_local_flow_topology: What flow pattern exists at the venous boundary?
failure_physics_chain.step_3_residence_time: How long does blood remain in the shunt?
failure_physics_chain.step_4_thrombus_initiation: How quickly does thrombus form from resident blood?
failure_physics_chain.step_5_clearance: How effectively does biological turnover clear deposits?
failure_physics_chain.step_6_sustained_drainage: How is CSF drainage maintained throughout?

historical_limitations.El_Shafi: Addressed step 1-3 via FLOW DIRECTION (retrograde) — passive, no coating, no active control
historical_limitations.Sinushunt: Addressed step 1 via PRESSURE DIFFERENTIAL — passive, no flow topology optimization
historical_limitations.modern_coatings: Address step 4 via SURFACE CHEMISTRY — passive, no flow control, no active valve
historical_limitations.fibrous_web: Addressed step 4 via PHYSICAL BARRIER — ventricular only, no venous interface

what_no_one_has_done: CONTROL LOCAL FLOW TOPOLOGY at the venous interface via device GEOMETRY (not just flow direction)
MINIMIZE RESIDENCE TIME by creating a flow regime that washes blood away before thrombus initiates
USE THE ENDOVASCULAR POSITION to create a shear environment that is fundamentally different from surgical shunts
COMBINE flow topology + surface chemistry + biological clearance in a SINGLE integrated venous-interface architecture

candidate_V7.name: VENOUS-INTERFACE FLOW-TOPOLOGY ARCHITECTURE
candidate_V7.core_mechanism: An endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt where the DEVICE GEOMETRY at the venous boundary creates a SPECIFIC LOCAL FLOW TOPOLOGY that: (a) minimizes blood residence time in the shunt lumen; (b) creates shear conditions that prevent thrombus initiation; (c) washes deposits toward the venous outflow before they accumulate; (d) maintains CSF drainage through a separate flow path that does not mix with the blood-washing zone.
candidate_V7.key_differentiation_from_historical: El-Shafei used RETROGRADE FLOW DIRECTION (CSF against blood) — a GLOBAL flow strategy. V7 uses LOCAL FLOW TOPOLOGY — device geometry creates specific shear and residence-time conditions at the venous interface. This is architecturally distinct: El-Shafei changes WHICH DIRECTION fluid flows; V7 changes HOW FLUID BEHAVES at the interface.
candidate_V7.key_differentiation_from_coatings: Coatings address SURFACE CHEMISTRY (preventing adhesion). V7 addresses FLOW PHYSICS (preventing deposition by minimizing residence time). These are different causal mechanisms: coatings work on what STICKS; flow topology works on what ARRIVES.

limitations_V7.L1: endovascular CSF shunt deployed percutaneously across dural venous sinus wall
limitations_V7.L2: device geometry at venous boundary creates a LOCAL FLOW TOPOLOGY characterized by: (a) high shear zone that prevents thrombus initiation; (b) short residence time for blood entering the shunt; (c) washout pattern that directs deposits toward venous outflow
limitations_V7.L3: CSF drainage path is SEPARATED from the blood-washing zone — CSF flows through a dedicated lumen that does not mix with the venous washout
limitations_V7.L4: the flow topology is ACHIEVED BY GEOMETRY (not by active pumping, not by coating, not by flow direction alone)
limitations_V7.L5: the geometry is eShunt-SPECIFIC — it arises from the endovascular transdural position creating a unique blood-CSF interface that surgical venous shunts cannot reproduce

candidate_V7.why_this_is_not_obvious: Historical venous shunts (El-Shafei) addressed anti-stagnation via GLOBAL flow direction. Modern coatings addressed anti-fouling via SURFACE chemistry. NEITHER addressed LOCAL FLOW TOPOLOGY at the venous interface. The eShunt's endovascular position creates a unique opportunity: the device can be GEOMETRICALLY SHAPED to create specific shear/residence-time conditions at the blood-CSF interface. This is a different causal mechanism (flow physics, not surface chemistry or global flow direction) and it requires the endovascular position (surgical shunts cannot create the same geometry).
candidate_V7.buyer_relevant_effect: If the flow topology minimizes blood residence time and prevents thrombus initiation, the shunt may maintain patency WITHOUT requiring drug-eluting coatings (which deplete) or active valves (which fail). This is a PASSIVE, PERMANENT solution to the F4 feedback loop — it breaks the causal chain at step 2-3 (flow topology → residence time) rather than at step 4 (thrombus initiation via coating) or step 1 (blood entry via valve).

evidence_needed: CFD simulation of flow topology at venous interface with different geometries
Comparison of residence time distributions: El-Shafei geometry vs eShunt geometry vs V7 geometry
Shear stress mapping at the blood-CSF interface
Does the flow topology actually prevent thrombus initiation under realistic venous pressure dynamics?
Is the geometry achievable in an endovascular device? (manufacturability)
simulation_needed: CFD model of eShunt venous boundary with parametric geometry variations
Particle tracking for residence time distribution
Thrombus initiation model coupled to flow field
Comparison vs El-Shafei retrograde flow and Sinushunt pressure-based flow
